messages:
olivia_support: Heads-up — AcmePay escalated: rerank endpoint returned different scores for identical inputs after last night's model rollout (redwood-rerank-v3). They sent a failing example where top-1 flipped to top-4. They also saw intermittent 504s during batch runs.

sara_cs: Thanks Olivia. Do we have the exact payload and model hash from their requests?

olivia_support: Pasted minimal repro from customer below. They say response `status: 200` for single items but batch calls (size 8-12) sometimes 504 and when 200 scores don't match pre-deploy baseline. Sample payload:```json
{"queries":[{"id":"q1","text":"best lightweight laptop"}],"candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"MacBook Air"},{"id":"c2","text":"XPS 13"}],"model":"redwood-rerank-v3","top_k":5}```

arjun_ml: Noted. v3 had a tokenization tweak + new softmax temp change (commit 9f3b2c). Could change relative ordering for borderline pairs. But 6-12% of queries flipping is concerning. Any diffs vs the pre-deploy deterministic seed/config?

olivia_support: Customer compared hashes against our sample; they used the hosted API endpoint and the exact same JSON. They logged request id: r-ACME-20260121-77.

miguel_sre: I pulled proxy traces for r-ACME-20260121-77 — backend responded 200, but we saw a slow KV cache miss for key prefix `prefix_kv:rerank:q1` ~180ms which pushed some batches to cross the 500ms SLO and upstream LB returning 504 on retries. I'll attach trace snippet.

deploy-bot: Deployment redwood-rerank-v3 rolled to prod at 2026-01-20T03:12:08Z (deploy id: dpl-20260120-12). Canary passed 2k queries.

henry_prod_eng: Miguel — slow KV misses explain the 504s, but not score deltas. Arjun, can quantization/softmax temp change create nondeterministic results across identical inputs?

arjun_ml: Quantization tweak was lossless for our regression eval, but the tokenization change could re-segment certain non-ascii punctuation and shift token boundaries, making logits differ. That would cause deterministic but different scores vs old model. However the customer says pre/post were run on same payload to same hosted model name — that should map to v3 now. Do we have archived inference outputs for v2 so we can diff logits?

sara_cs: I created a save point: request ids r-ACME-20260119-33 (pre-deploy) and r-ACME-20260121-77 (post). Saved full JSON responses to /var/archives/rerank_acme/ in case we need to share.

olivia_support: Customer wants rollback if this is a regression impacting business. They saw click-through drop when top result changed. Also mention of a `401` on a follow-up — they rotated API key and then got `invalid_api_key` while using the old key in a scheduled job. Billing isn't implicated yet.

henry_prod_eng: Action items I'm proposing: (1) reproduce locally: run both v2 and v3 against the customer's exact payload using the archived inputs; (2) compare tokenization and logits; (3) check if we can hotfix by reverting the tokenization tweak or mapping model alias to v2 for this customer while we investigate.

arjun_ml: I'll run a diff job now. Quick commands for repro I used:```bash
# fetch archived payload
aws s3 cp s3://rerank-acme/1912468000/payload.json - | jq .
# run against model binaries
./bin/infer --model models/redwood-rerank-v2 --input payload.json > out_v2.json
./bin/infer --model models/redwood-rerank-v3 --input payload.json > out_v3.json
# diff logits
jq '.results[].scores' out_v2.json > s2 && jq '.results[].scores' out_v3.json > s3 && diff s2 s3```

miguel_sre: I can patch the LB to raise the retry timeout for this customer for now and investigate KV cache warmups. I'll also look for correlation between batch size and 504 rate.

olivia_support: Customer notes one more weird thing: sometimes individual candidate texts returned with trailing whitespace in our response, which changed tokenization downstream. Example: "c1":"MacBook Air " (note trailing space). That could explain resegmentation.

arjun_ml: Good catch. We sanitize candidate text on ingest but v3 might have missed a trim during candidate preprocessing. I'll run a quick unit test for whitespace normalization.

henry_prod_eng: If whitespace bug confirmed, mitigations: hotfix to trim inputs in preprocessing + quick rollout, or alias their model endpoint back to v2 while we ship fix. Which is lower risk?

sara_cs: For SLA and customer trust, aliasing them to v2 (temporary) plus a public postmortem sounds safest. I'll coordinate comms if we switch.

olivia_support: Customer wanted repro steps to validate on their side. Please include exact endpoint + header sample.```http
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <CUSTOMER_KEY>
Content-Type: application/json

{payload as above}```

miguel_sre: Assigned to oncall to check KV cache metrics and LB retries: pinging @miguel_sre-oncall. Also scheduling a brief during-incident channel in #incidents.

arjun_ml: I ran diffs — there are deterministic differences in logits for ~8% of candidates, correlated with token splits at punctuation and trailing spaces. I think this is tokenization/preprocessing regression. Creating PR to enforce trimming and add tests.

henry_prod_eng: Ok let's do two-step: 1) alias AcmePay to redwood-rerank-v2 for now (sara to coordinate), 2) deploy PR to fix trimming + unit tests, run internal eval, 3) rollout v3.1 and monitor.

olivia_support: Customer update: if we can alias them quickly they'd prefer that while we fix. They want an ETA within 4 hours.

sara_cs: I'll request alias now and confirm when completed. Also prepping a support note and apologetic comms. :+1:

deploy-bot: Alias request processed: acmepay -> redwood-rerank-v2 at 2026-01-21T09:12:03Z (task id: alias-887).

olivia_support: Thanks team — will update customer once alias is confirmed and keep thread open. Follow-ups: please paste PR link and perf check when available.
